## Segment summary
This segment documents Day 2 of building an AI robot companion named "Mac," showcasing its evolution from a simple talking device to a more advanced model with object and face-tracking capabilities. The creator, Aykhan, demonstrates the robot's new features, including its ability to observe its surroundings, track faces and held objects, and perform body movements using SG90 servos, while also showing the components used and the 3D modeling process involved.

## Events
<0:00.0> - The video opens with a close-up of a white 3D-printed robot head with exposed wiring, sitting on a desk next to a purple cutting mat. A person with curly hair and glasses is partially visible on the right.
<0:01.3> - The camera focuses on the robot head, which now has a small screen displaying two glowing green squares, indicating it is powered on.
<0:02.7> - The scene cuts to a wider shot showing the creator, Aykhan, sitting in a black office chair at his desk.
<0:04.0> - The camera pans down to show a white keyboard, a black mouse, and blue-handled pliers on the purple cutting mat.
<0:05.3> - The creator holds up the robot, now labeled "Mac" by on-screen text, showing its small size.
<0:06.7> - The creator displays "version 1" of the robot, which has a different screen display.
<0:08.0> - The creator shows "version 1.5" of the robot, which has a new body and can move its head.
<0:09.3> - The robot is shown on the desk, and the text indicates it can now "observe everything around him."
<0:10.7> - The robot's camera is shown tracking the creator's face, which is highlighted with a green box and labeled "human."
<0:12.0> - The robot's camera is shown tracking a pen held by the creator, which is highlighted with a green box and labeled "pen."
<0:13.3> - The creator holds up a pen in front of the robot, demonstrating its ability to track "whatever I'm holding."
<0:14.7> - The robot's head is shown moving, with text indicating this is "for body movements."
<0:16.0> - The creator holds up two blue SG90 servos, which are identified as the components "for body movements."
<0:17.3> - The robot is shown with its camera module highlighted, and the text identifies it as an "ESP32S3 CAM."
<0:18.7> - The creator is shown working on the robot's assembly, connecting wires and components.
<0:20.0> - The creator continues assembling the robot, with text indicating they spent time "putting all together."
<0:21.4> - The creator continues assembling the robot, with text indicating they didn't know "that there are gonna be" further changes or complications.

## Segment summary
A person is shown building and programming a small robotic device called "Mac" using a computer. The segment begins with the physical assembly of the robot's hardware, followed by the user launching multiple AI agents on their Mac to simultaneously develop the robot's movement logic, face-tracking capabilities, and a companion website. The final frames show the robot's face displaying different expressions in real-time as controlled by the software, and conclude with a call to action for viewers to comment "MINIBOT" for a project link.
